title.zh: 卷五十二 吳書七 張顧諸葛步傳
title.en: Volume 52: Book of Wu 7 - Biographies of Zhang, Gu, Zhuge, and Bu
title.raw: 卷五十二 吳書七 張顧諸葛步傳 Volume 52: Book of Wu 7 - Biographies of Zhang, Gu, Zhuge, and Bu

sentences.zh: 張昭字子布，彭城人也。

translations.literal: Zhang Zhao, courtesy name Zibu, was a man of Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhao, styled Zibu, hailed from Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 少好學，善隸書，從白侯子安受《左氏春秋》，博覽眾書，與琅邪趙昱、東海王朗俱發名友善。

translations.literal: In youth he loved learning, was skilled at clerical script, received Zuo's Spring and Autumn from Bai Hou Zi'an, read widely among texts, and together with Zhao Yu of Langye and Wang Lang of Donghai rose to fame as friendly associates.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he loved books, wrote a fine clerical hand, studied the Zuo commentary under Bai Hou Zi’an, read omnivorously, and made his name alongside Zhao Yu of Langye and Wang Lang of Donghai.

sentences.zh: 弱冠察孝廉，不就。

translations.literal: At the capping age he was investigated as filially pious and incorrupt but did not take office.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended as filially pious and incorrupt at his capping, he refused appointment.

sentences.zh: 與朗共論舊君諱事，州裡才士陳琳等皆稱善之。

translations.literal: Together with Lang he debated the affair of tabooing former lords; talented men of the commandery such as Chen Lin all praised them.
translations.idiomatic: He argued with Wang Lang over taboos for former rulers; local talents such as Chen Lin praised his performance.

sentences.zh: 〈时汝南主簿应劭议宜为旧君讳，论者皆互有异同，事在《风俗通》。

translations.literal: 〈At that time Ying Shao, chief clerk of Runan, argued one ought taboo former lords; debaters differed from one another—the affair is in Fengsu tong.〉
translations.idiomatic: (Ying Shao of Runan had argued for tabooing former masters; the dispute is recorded in the Fengsu tong.)

sentences.zh: 昭著论曰：“客有见大国之议，士君子之论，云起元建武已来，旧君名讳五十六人，以为后生不得协也。

translations.literal: Zhao composed a treatise stating: "A guest saw the great state's deliberation and gentlemen's discourse, saying that from Yuanjian Wu onward there are fifty-six former lords' tabooed names, holding that later generations may not harmonize with them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhao wrote that someone cited court debate: since Guangwu, fifty-six rulers’ names were taboo—students must never echo those syllables.

sentences.zh: 取乎经论，譬诸行事，义高辞丽，甚可嘉羡。

translations.literal: Taking from the classics and commentaries, comparing to deeds performed, the righteousness is lofty and phrases lovely—greatly to be admired.
translations.idiomatic: Drawn from canonical gloss and matched to precedent, the rhetoric glows—yet something troubles me.

sentences.zh: 愚意褊浅，窃有疑焉。

translations.literal: My foolish thought is narrow and shallow—I privately harbor doubt.
translations.idiomatic: Forgive a shallow mind—I cannot quite agree.

sentences.zh: 盖乾坤剖分，万物定形，肇有父子君臣之经。

translations.literal: In general when Heaven and Earth split apart and the myriad things fixed their forms, there began the constant pattern of father and son, lord and minister.
translations.idiomatic: Once heaven and earth divided and creation took shape, the bonds of parent and child, ruler and subject, appeared.

sentences.zh: 故圣人顺天之性，制礼尚敬，在三之义，君实食之，在丧之哀，君亲临之，厚莫重焉，恩莫大焉，诚臣子所尊仰，万夫所天恃，焉得而同之哉？

translations.literal: Therefore the sage complies with heaven's nature, institutes ritual and esteems reverence; in the duty of the three the lord truly nourishes; in mourning's grief the lord personally attends—the thickness cannot be heavier, the grace cannot be greater—truly what ministers and sons revere and myriad men rely on—how can they be equated?
translations.idiomatic: The sage fashioned ritual from heaven’s nature: lords feed us under the “three that endure”; they mourn with us—nothing outweighs that debt. How can subjects rank them with ordinary kin?

sentences.zh: 然亲亲有衰，尊尊有杀，故礼服上不尽高祖，下不尽玄孙。

translations.literal: Yet intimacy toward kin has degrees of decline; reverence toward superiors has steps of reduction—therefore mourning garments upward do not exhaust great-great-grandfather, downward do not exhaust great-great-grandchild.
translations.idiomatic: Yet kinship weakens by generation and mourning scales down—hence hemp stops short of the fifth grandfather above and the fifth grandson below.

sentences.zh: 又传记四世而缌麻，服之穷也；

translations.literal: Moreover transmitted records: four generations and thin hemp—end of garments;
translations.idiomatic: Genealogies say after four generations one wears only thin hemp.

sentences.zh: 五世袒免，降杀同姓也；

translations.literal: five generations shed turban and fringe—reduced severity toward same surname;
translations.idiomatic: After five generations one merely bares head and wrist—the mourning grade fades even within the clan.

sentences.zh: 六世而亲属竭矣。

translations.literal: six generations and kinship ties are exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: By the sixth generation kinship ends.

sentences.zh: 又曲礼有不逮事之义则不讳，不讳者，盖名之谓，属绝之义，不拘於协，况乃古君五十六哉！

translations.literal: Moreover the Summary of Etiquette has the sense that if one did not succeed to service there is no taboo—no taboo refers to personal names; meaning of severed connection is not bound by harmonizing—how much more fifty-six ancient lords!
translations.idiomatic: The Summary of Etiquette also exempts those who never served a lord from tabooing him—that ends obligation to a mere name. If distant kin need not rhyme away syllables, why taboo scores of dead kings?

sentences.zh: 邾子会盟，季友来归，不称其名，咸书字者，是时鲁人嘉之也。

translations.literal: The lord of Zhu at covenant assembly, Jiyou came to return—his name was not called; all were written with style—at that time the people of Lu praised it.
translations.idiomatic: When the Zhu ruler met allies and Jiyou came home, the classic wrote his style, not his name—Lu admired the tact.

sentences.zh: 何解臣子为君父讳乎？

translations.literal: How explain ministers and sons tabooing for lord and father?
translations.idiomatic: So why insist clerks taboo every syllable of old patrons?

sentences.zh: 周穆王讳满，至定王时有王孙满者，其为大夫，是臣协君也。

translations.literal: King Mu of Zhou tabooed Man; when it reached King Ding there was Wangsun Man who was grand officer—that is a minister harmonizing with his lord.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou King Mu banned “Man,” yet under King Ding a minister Wangsun Man served—a subject bore the sovereign’s taboo.

sentences.zh: 又厉王讳胡，及庄王之子名胡，其比众多。

translations.literal: Moreover King Li tabooed Hu; and among King Zhuang's sons one was named Hu—their parallels are numerous.
translations.idiomatic: King Li banned “Hu,” yet Zhuang’s son was Hu—examples abound.

sentences.zh: 夫类事建议，经有明据，传有徵案，然后进攻退守，万无奔北，垂示百世，永无咎失。

translations.literal: When grouping affairs and proposing counsel, the classics have clear proofs and the commentaries verifiable cases—then advancing attack or retreating defense never flees north in defeat; displaying for a hundred generations, never failing or missing.
translations.idiomatic: Advice must rest on canonical proof and commentary precedent—otherwise posterity laughs.

sentences.zh: 今应劭虽上尊旧君之名，而下无所断齐，犹归之疑云。

translations.literal: Now although Ying Shao upward honors former lords' names, downward he decides nothing uniform—still it returns to doubtful clouds.
translations.idiomatic: Ying Shao honors old masters’ names yet sets no clear rule below—it stays muddled.

sentences.zh: 曲礼之篇，疑事无质，观省上下，阙义自证，文辞可为，倡而不法，将来何观？

translations.literal: The Summary of Etiquette chapter—doubtful matters lack substance; observing above and below, missing righteousness proves itself—literary phrasing may be composed, advocated but not lawful—what will the future behold?
translations.idiomatic: The Summary of Etiquette passages he cites prove nothing; pretty words without law teach nothing.

sentences.zh: 言声一放，犹拾瀋也，过辞在前，悔其何追！”〉

translations.literal: Once speech is released it is like scooping bilge—faulty phrases come first, what regret can follow!"〉
translations.idiomatic: Loosen tongues and you scoop sewage—bad rhetoric spreads before you can repent.”)

sentences.zh: 刺史陶謙舉茂才，不應，謙以為輕己，遂見拘執。

translations.literal: Inspector Tao Qian nominated him outstanding talent; he did not respond—Qian thought he slighted himself and thereupon had him seized.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Tao Qian nominated him for office; when Zhang Zhao declined, Tao felt insulted and jailed him.

sentences.zh: 昱傾身營救，方以得免。

translations.literal: Yu threw himself into arranging rescue—only then did he obtain release.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Yu spent himself on bail until Zhang Zhao went free.

sentences.zh: 漢末大亂，徐方士民多避難揚土，昭皆南渡江。

translations.literal: At the end of Han great chaos arose; gentlemen and commoners of Xu region mostly fled calamity to Yang territory—Zhao all crossed the river south.
translations.idiomatic: Late Han turmoil drove Xu refugees south—Zhang Zhao crossed with them.

sentences.zh: 孫策創業，命昭為長史、撫軍中郎將，升堂拜母，如比肩之舊，文武之事，一以委昭。

translations.literal: When Sun Ce founded the enterprise he appointed Zhao chief clerk and General of the Household Gentlemen Who Pacifies the Army, ascended the hall to bow to his mother as with old peers shoulder to shoulder—civil and military affairs he wholly entrusted to Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ce named him chief clerk and general who pacifies the army, treated him like family before Lady Wu, and handed him every civil and military file.

sentences.zh: 〈吴书曰：策得昭甚悦，谓曰：“吾方有事四方，以士人贤者上，吾於子不得轻矣。

translations.literal: [Wu shu] states: Ce gained Zhao and was very pleased, saying to him: "I am about to have affairs in the four quarters—with scholar worthies above I cannot treat you lightly.
translations.idiomatic: (The Wu shu: Sun Ce rejoiced: “I mean to stride the empire—among scholar-advisers I must honor you.

sentences.zh: ”乃上为校尉，待以师友之礼。〉

translations.literal: " Thereupon he promoted him to colonel and treated him with the ritual of teacher and friend.〉
translations.idiomatic: ” So he raised him to colonel and courted him as mentor.)

sentences.zh: 昭每得北方士大夫書疏，專歸美於昭，昭欲嘿而不宣則懼有私，宣之則恐非宜，進退不安。

translations.literal: Whenever Zhao obtained letters from northern gentlemen-officials they exclusively attributed praise to Zhao; Zhao wished to keep silent and not announce yet feared there was partiality; announcing yet feared it was not appropriate—advancing and retreating were uneasy.
translations.idiomatic: Northern letters flattered Zhang Zhao alone; silence seemed sneaky, publication awkward—he squirmed either way.

sentences.zh: 策聞之，歡笑曰："昔管仲相齊，一則仲父，二則仲父，而桓公為霸者宗。

translations.literal: When Ce heard it he laughed happily and said: "Formerly Guan Zhong served Qi—first 'Father Zhong,' second 'Father Zhong,' yet Duke Huan became hegemon-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ce laughed: “Guan Zhong called Huan Gong ‘Father’ twice—and Huan became hegemon.

sentences.zh: 今子布賢，我能用之，其功名獨不在我乎!"，

translations.literal: Now Zibu is worthy—if I can employ him, will the merit and fame alone not rest with me!"
translations.idiomatic: Zibu is worthy; if I use him well, the glory is surely mine!”

sentences.zh: 策臨亡，以弟權托昭，昭率群僚立而輔之。

translations.literal: When Ce faced death he entrusted his younger brother Quan to Zhao; Zhao led the host of officials to establish and assist him.
translations.idiomatic: Dying, Sun Ce left Sun Quan to Zhang Zhao, who enthroned him with the whole civil staff.

sentences.zh: 〈吴历曰：策谓昭曰：“若仲谋不任事者，君便自取之。

translations.literal: [Wu li] states: Ce said to Zhao: "If Zhongmou cannot bear the charge, you yourself take it.
translations.idiomatic: (The Wu li: Sun Ce told Zhang Zhao: “If Zhongmou fails, take the throne yourself.

sentences.zh: 正复不克捷，缓步西归，亦无所虑。”〉

translations.literal: Even if you cannot achieve victory, walk slowly west homeward—there is likewise nothing to worry about."〉
translations.idiomatic: If all else fails, retreat west—no shame.”)

sentences.zh: 上表漢室，下移屬城，中外將校，各令奉職，權悲感未視事，昭謂權曰："夫為人後者，貴能負荷先軌，克昌堂構，以成勳業也。

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial to the Han court and issued orders downward to dependent cities; Chinese and foreign generals and colonels each had orders to uphold duty—Quan grieved and had not yet assumed affairs; Zhao said to Quan: "One who becomes another's successor esteems being able to shoulder former tracks, expand the hall's construction, and complete merit and enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: He petitioned the Han, ordered every garrison, while Sun Quan still wept; Zhang Zhao said: “An heir must shoulder his brother’s work and finish the house God gave him.

sentences.zh: 方今天下鼎沸，群盜滿山，孝廉何得寢伏哀戚，肆匹夫之情哉？

translations.literal: Now the realm boils like a cauldron; bandits fill the mountains—how can a filially pious and incorrupt youth lie hidden in grief and indulge private man's feeling?
translations.idiomatic: The world seethes with rebels—how can you hide in mourning like a common mourner?

sentences.zh: "乃身自扶權上馬，陳兵而出，然後眾心知有所歸。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he personally supported Quan onto a horse, arrayed troops and went forth—only afterward did the host's hearts know what to attach to.
translations.idiomatic: ” He hoisted Sun Quan into the saddle, paraded the army, and gave the realm something to follow.

sentences.zh: 昭復為權長史，授任如前。

translations.literal: Zhao again became chief clerk for Quan, commission as before.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhao served again as chief clerk with the same powers.

sentences.zh: 〈吴书曰：是时天下分裂，擅命者众。

translations.literal: [Wu shu] states: At that time the realm was split; those who grasped command were many.
translations.idiomatic: (The Wu shu: the empire shattered into warlords.)

sentences.zh: 孙策莅事日浅，恩泽未洽，一旦倾陨，士民狼狈，颇有同异。

translations.literal: Sun Ce had handled affairs few days; grace and favor had not yet permeated—once he suddenly fell, officers and commoners were in disarray and partly agreed and partly differed.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Ce had ruled briefly; favor had not sunk in—when he died overnight, people panicked and opinions split.

sentences.zh: 及昭辅权，绥抚百姓，诸侯宾旅寄寓之士，得用自安。

translations.literal: When Zhao assisted Quan he soothed the hundred surnames; gentlemen-officials of the feudal lords and traveling guests lodging abroad obtained employment and settled themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhao calmed the people and found posts for every refugee scholar.

sentences.zh: 权每出征，留昭镇守，领幕府事。

translations.literal: Whenever Quan campaigned forth he left Zhao to guard and hold, directing headquarters affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Sun Quan marched, Zhang Zhao held headquarters.

sentences.zh: 后黄巾贼起，昭讨平之。

translations.literal: Later Yellow Turban bandits arose and Zhao campaigned and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: When Yellow Turbans flared, Zhang Zhao crushed them.

sentences.zh: 权征合肥，命昭别讨匡琦，又督领诸将，攻破豫章贼率周凤等於南城。

translations.literal: Quan campaigned against Hefei and ordered Zhao separately to campaign against Kuangqi; again he supervised and led the generals, defeating Yuzhang bandit leaders Zhou Feng and others at Nancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan besieged Hefei while Zhang Zhao struck Kuangqi, then led generals to smash Zhou Feng’s bandits at Nancheng.

sentences.zh: 自此希复将帅，常在左右，为谋谟臣。

translations.literal: From this he rarely again acted as commander—always at the right and left as planning minister.
translations.idiomatic: After that he seldom commanded troops—he stayed at Sun Quan’s side as strategist.

sentences.zh: 权以昭旧臣，待遇尤重。〉

translations.literal: Quan because Zhao was an old minister treated him especially generously.〉
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan favored him as an elder statesman.)

sentences.zh: 後劉備表權行車騎將軍，昭為軍師。

translations.literal: Later Liu Bei memorialized Quan as acting chariots-and-cavalry general; Zhao became army adviser.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Bei petitioned Sun Quan as acting chariots-and-cavalry general, Zhang Zhao became army adviser.

sentences.zh: 權每田獵，常乘馬射虎，虎常突前攀持馬鞍。

translations.literal: Whenever Quan hunted fields he often rode horses shooting tigers—the tiger always burst forward climbing and holding the saddle.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan loved to hunt tigers on horseback—beasts often leaped at his saddle.

sentences.zh: 昭變色而前曰："將軍何有當爾?夫為人君者，謂能駕御英雄，驅使群賢，豈謂馳逐於原野，校勇於猛獸者乎？

translations.literal: Zhao changed color and stepped forward saying: "How can the general act thus? One who is lord of men is called able to drive heroes and dispatch worthies—does it mean racing the wilderness and measuring valor against fierce beasts?
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhao stepped up pale: “What sort of ruler races beasts in the brush?

sentences.zh: 如有一旦之患，奈天下笑何?"權謝昭曰："年少慮事不遠，以此慚君。

translations.literal: If there should be one morning's misfortune, what of the realm's laughter?" Quan apologized to Zhao saying: "Youth's consideration does not reach far—thereby I feel shame before you.
translations.idiomatic: One misstep and the world mocks you.” Sun Quan apologized: “I am young and shortsighted.”

sentences.zh: "然猶不能已，乃作射虎車，為方目，間不置蓋，一人為御，自於中射之。

translations.literal: " Yet he still could not stop; thereupon he made a tiger-shooting cart with square eyes, gaps without placing a canopy—one man drove while he himself shot from within.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he kept hunting—he built a screened chariot with square peepholes, a driver outside, himself shooting within.

sentences.zh: 時有逸群之獸，輒復犯車，而權每手擊以為樂。

translations.literal: At times there were beasts surpassing the herd—they again charged the cart; yet Quan often personally struck them for pleasure.
translations.idiomatic: Monstrous brutes charged the car; Sun Quan thrashed them for sport.

sentences.zh: 昭雖諫爭，常笑而不答。

translations.literal: Although Zhao remonstrated and contended, Quan constantly smiled and did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhao argued; Sun Quan only smiled.

sentences.zh: 魏黃初二年，遣使者邢貞拜權為吳王。

translations.literal: Wei Huangchu second year they dispatched envoy Xing Zhen to invest Quan as King of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: In Wei Huangchu 2 envoy Xing Zhen came to enfeoff Sun Quan as king of Wu.

sentences.zh: 貞入門，不下車。

translations.literal: When Zhen entered the gate he did not dismount from the cart.
translations.idiomatic: Xing Zhen rode through the gate without alighting.

sentences.zh: 昭謂貞曰："夫禮無不敬，故法無不行。

translations.literal: Zhao said to Zhen: "In ritual nothing is without reverence—therefore in law nothing fails to execute.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhao said: “Ritual demands respect—law follows.

sentences.zh: 而君敢自尊大，豈以江南寡弱，無方寸之刃故乎！

translations.literal: Yet you dare esteem yourself great—is it because Jiangnan is weak and lacks a blade one inch square!
translations.idiomatic: You swagger because you think the south unarmed?

sentences.zh: "貞即遽下車。

translations.literal: " Zhen immediately hastily dismounted.
translations.idiomatic: ” Xing Zhen scrambled down.

sentences.zh: 拜昭為綏遠將軍，封由拳侯。

translations.literal: He invested Zhao as General Who Pacifies the Distance and enfeoffed him Marquis of Youquan.
translations.idiomatic: The court named Zhang Zhao General Who Pacifies the Distance and marquis of Youquan.

sentences.zh: 〈吴录曰：昭与孙绍、滕胤、郑礼等，采周、汉，撰定朝仪。〉

translations.literal: [Wu lu] states: Zhao together with Sun Shao, Teng Yin, Zheng Li and others drew on Zhou and Han and compiled settled court ritual.〉
translations.idiomatic: (The Wu lu: Zhang Zhao, Sun Shao, Teng Yin, and Zheng Li codified court ceremony from Zhou and Han.)

sentences.zh: 權於武昌，臨釣台，飲酒大醉。

translations.literal: Quan was at Wuchang, approached the fishing terrace, drank wine and was greatly drunk.
translations.idiomatic: At Wuchang Sun Quan drank himself stupid on the fishing terrace.

sentences.zh: 權使人以水灑群臣曰："今日酣飲，惟醉墮台中，乃當止耳。

translations.literal: Quan had people sprinkle water on the host of ministers saying: "Today we drink deep—only when drunk and fallen into the terrace ought we stop.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered aides to splash ministers: “We stop only when someone falls off this terrace drunk.”

sentences.zh: "昭正色不言，出外車中坐。

translations.literal: " Zhao with stern color did not speak—went out and sat in the carriage.
translations.idiomatic: ” Zhang Zhao sat mute in his coach.

sentences.zh: 權遣人呼昭還，謂曰："為共作樂耳，公何為怒乎？

translations.literal: Quan dispatched people summoning Zhao back, saying to him: "We merely made merry together—why did the duke grow angry?
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan called him back: “We were only celebrating—why anger?

sentences.zh: "昭對曰："昔紂為糟丘酒池長夜之飲，當時亦以為樂，不以為惡也。

translations.literal: " Zhao replied saying: "Formerly Zhou made lees-hill and wine-pool for all-night drinking—at that time they also thought it pleasure and did not think it evil.
translations.idiomatic: ” Zhang Zhao answered: “Zhou of Shang held orgies on his wine hill—his court called it fun.”

sentences.zh: "權默然。

translations.literal: " Quan was silent.
translations.idiomatic: ” Sun Quan fell silent.

sentences.zh: 有慚色，遂罷酒。

translations.literal: Having a shameful color he thereupon stopped the wine.
translations.idiomatic: Ashamed, he ended the banquet.

sentences.zh: 初，權當置丞相，眾議歸昭。

translations.literal: At first when Quan was about to appoint a chief minister the host of deliberation returned the choice to Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: When Sun Quan first chose a chancellor, everyone picked Zhang Zhao.

sentences.zh: 權曰："方今多事，職統者責重，非所以優之也。

translations.literal: Quan said: "Nowadays affairs are many; the one who grasps duty bears heavy responsibility—it is not therefore to favor him.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan said: “Times are hard—the chancellor’s burden is cruel; I am not favoring anyone.”

sentences.zh: "後孫邵卒，百寮復舉昭，權曰："孤豈為子布有愛乎?領丞相事煩，而此公性剛，所言不從，怨咎將興，非所以益之也。

translations.literal: " Later when Sun Shao died the hundred officials again nominated Zhao; Quan said: "How could I bear love toward Zibu? Bearing chief minister affairs is vexing—yet this gentleman's nature is rigid; what he speaks is not followed—resentment and blame will arise—it is not therefore to benefit him.
translations.idiomatic: ” After Sun Shao died they nominated Zhang Zhao again; Sun Quan said: “It is not fondness—his temper is stiff; if I ignore him we quarrel.”

sentences.zh: "乃用顧雍。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he employed Gu Yong.
translations.idiomatic: ” So he picked Gu Yong.

sentences.zh: 權既稱尊號，昭以老病，上還官位及所統領。

translations.literal: After Quan had assumed the imperial title Zhao because of old age and illness upward returned office rank and what he commanded and led.
translations.idiomatic: Once Sun Quan declared himself emperor, Zhang Zhao, old and ill, returned his seals.

sentences.zh: 〈江表传曰：权既即尊位，请会百官，归功周瑜。

translations.literal: [Jiangbiao zhuan] states: After Quan had assumed the supreme position he invited assembly of the hundred officials and attributed merit to Zhou Yu.
translations.idiomatic: (The Jiangbiao zhuan: enthroned, Sun Quan toasted Zhou Yu first.)

sentences.zh: 昭举笏欲褒赞功德，未及言，权曰：“如张公之计，今已乞食矣。

translations.literal: Zhao raised his tablet wishing to praise merit and virtue; before he spoke Quan said: "According to Lord Zhang's plan, today we would already be begging food.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhao lifted his hu to praise Sun Quan—who cut him off: “Had I listened to you I would beg for supper.”

sentences.zh: ”昭大惭，伏地流汗。

translations.literal: " Zhao was greatly ashamed, prostrated on the ground sweating.
translations.idiomatic: ” Zhang Zhao dropped sweating.

sentences.zh: 昭忠謇亮直，有大臣节，权敬重之，然所以不相昭者，盖以昔駮周瑜、鲁肃等议为非也。

translations.literal: Zhao was loyal, blunt, and straightforward with great ministers' integrity—Quan respected him—yet the reason he did not appoint Zhao chief minister is because he formerly refuted Zhou Yu, Lu Su and others' counsel as wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhao was bluntly loyal; Sun Quan honored him yet withheld the chancellorship because Zhang had opposed Zhou Yu and Lu Su.

sentences.zh: 臣松之以为张昭劝迎曹公，所存岂不远乎？

translations.literal: Your servant Songzhi considers: Zhang Zhao urged welcoming Duke Cao—was not what he preserved far-reaching?
translations.idiomatic: Pei Songzhi asks: Zhang Zhao urged yielding to Cao Cao—was that vision not long?

sentences.zh: 夫其扬休正色，委质孙氏，诚以厄运初遘，涂炭方始，自策及权，才略足辅，是以尽诚匡弼，以成其业，上籓汉室，下保民物；

translations.literal: As for his displaying dignity with correct color, committing substance to the Sun clan—it was truly because misfortune had first met and scorching was just beginning—from Ce to Quan talent and strategy sufficed to assist—therefore he exhausted sincerity in aiding and supporting to complete their enterprise; upward he fenced the Han house, downward he preserved people and things;
translations.idiomatic: He lent the Suns full loyalty because chaos had just begun—Sun Ce and Sun Quan could use his counsel to shield the Han symbol and the people.

sentences.zh: 鼎峙之计，本非其志也。

translations.literal: The plan of tripod standoff was originally not his intent.
translations.idiomatic: Partition was never his first choice.

sentences.zh: 曹公仗顺而起，功以义立，冀以清一诸华，拓平荆郢，大定之机，在於此会。

translations.literal: Duke Cao relied on compliance to rise; merit was established through righteousness; he hoped thereby to unify all Chinese, broaden peace to Jing and Ying—the great settling opportunity lay in this conjunction.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao claimed the mandate to reunify north China and the middle Yangzi—the moment favored unity.

sentences.zh: 若使昭议获从，则六合为一，岂有兵连祸结，遂为战国之弊哉！

translations.literal: If Zhao's counsel had been followed then the six regions would have become one—how could weapons have linked and calamity knotted, ending in Warring States harm!
translations.idiomatic: Had Zhang Zhao prevailed, one empire might have returned—no endless wars.

sentences.zh: 虽无功於孙氏，有大当於天下矣。

translations.literal: Although without merit toward the Sun clan there was great correctness toward the realm.
translations.idiomatic: It would have helped China more than the Sun house.

sentences.zh: 昔窦融归汉，与国升降；

translations.literal: Formerly Dou Rong submitted to Han—rising and falling with the state;
translations.idiomatic: Dou Rong joined the Han and rose with it.

sentences.zh: 张鲁降魏，赏延于世。

translations.literal: Zhang Lu surrendered to Wei—reward extended through the generations.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Lu yielded to Wei and his heirs thrived.

sentences.zh: 况权举全吴，望风顺服，宠灵之厚，其可测量哉！

translations.literal: How much more Quan raising all Wu and looking to the wind to submit—thick favor and numinous grace—can it be measured!
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan offering Wu intact could have won vast favor.

sentences.zh: 然则昭为人谋，岂不忠且正乎！〉

translations.literal: Yet thus Zhao planning for others—was he not loyal and correct!〉
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhao’s advice served loyalty and right.)

sentences.zh: 更拜輔吳將軍，班亞三司，改封婁侯，食邑萬戶。

translations.literal: He was again appointed General Who Assists Wu, rank second to the Three Offices, enfeoffed Marquis of Lou, food estate ten thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: He became General Who Assists Wu, rank just below the Three Ducal ministers, marquis of Lou with ten thousand households.

sentences.zh: 在裡宅無事，乃著《春秋左氏傳》解及《論語》注。

translations.literal: In village residence without affairs he thereupon composed exegesis on Zuo's Spring and Autumn Transmission and commentary on the Analects.
translations.idiomatic: Retired at home he wrote a Zuo commentary and Analects glosses.

sentences.zh: 權嘗問衛尉嚴畯："寧念小時所暗書不？

translations.literal: Quan once asked Commandant of the Guards Yan Jun: "Do you still remember the books you recited in youth?
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan asked Yan Jun whether he still knew his childhood texts.

sentences.zh: "畯因誦《孝經》"仲尼居"。

translations.literal: " Jun thereupon recited the Classic of Filial Piety "Zhongni dwelt".
translations.idiomatic: ” Yan Jun began the Classic of Filial Piety with “Zhongni dwelt…”

sentences.zh: 昭曰："嚴畯鄙生，臣請為陛下誦之。

translations.literal: Zhao said: "Yan Jun is a rustic scholar—your servant requests to recite for Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhao said: “Yan Jun is crude—let me recite for you.”

sentences.zh: "乃誦"君子之事上"，鹹以昭為知所誦。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he recited "The gentleman's serving superiors"—all considered Zhao knew what was fitting to recite.
translations.idiomatic: ” He chose “The gentleman’s serving superiors”—everyone saw the point.

sentences.zh: 昭每朝見，辭氣壯厲，義形於色，曾以直言逆旨，中不進見。

translations.literal: Whenever Zhao attended court audience his phrasing was vigorous and stern, righteousness showing in his expression—once because of straight speech opposing intent he centrally did not advance to audience.
translations.idiomatic: At court Zhang Zhao’s voice cut; once Sun Quan barred him for blunt words.

sentences.zh: 後蜀使來，稱蜀德美，而群臣莫拒，權歎曰："使張公在坐，彼不折則廢，安復自誇乎?"明日，遣中使勞問，因請見昭。

translations.literal: Later when Shu envoys came praising Shu's virtue beautifully yet none of the host of ministers refuted them—Quan sighed saying: "If Lord Zhang had been seated they would not have been broken or exhausted—how again could they boast themselves?" The next day he dispatched inner attendant to console and inquire, thereby requesting audience with Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: When Shu envoys boasted and Wu had no answer, Sun Quan sighed: “Had Zhang Zhao been here they would have fled mute.” Next day he sent envoys to coax Zhang Zhao back.

sentences.zh: 昭避席謝，權跪止之。

translations.literal: Zhao vacated his mat and apologized—Quan knelt to stop him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhao rose to apologize; Sun Quan knelt to stop him.

sentences.zh: 昭坐定，仰曰："昔太后、桓王不以老臣屬陛下，而以陛下屬老臣，是以思盡臣節，以報厚恩。

translations.literal: When Zhao sat settled he looked up saying: "Formerly the Dowager and Prince Huan did not consign the old minister to Your Majesty but consigned Your Majesty to the old minister—therefore I thought to exhaust ministerial integrity to repay thick grace.
translations.idiomatic: Seated, Zhang Zhao said: “Lady Wu and Prince Ce left you to me—not me to you—so I owe you perfect loyalty.

sentences.zh: 使泯沒之後，有可稱述，而意慮淺短，違逆盛旨，自分幽淪，長棄溝壑，不圖復蒙引見，得奉帷幄。

translations.literal: If after extinction I should have something worth narrating—yet thought and consideration were shallow and short, opposing and rejecting great intent—I divided myself to sink into oblivion, long cast into ditches and gorges—I did not plan again to receive summons and audience, obtain attendance within the tent curtain.
translations.idiomatic: I expected to die disgraced for defying you—never dreamed you would recall me to council.

sentences.zh: 然臣愚心所以事國，志在忠益，畢命而已。

translations.literal: Yet this foolish minister's heart by which he serves the state lies in aiming at loyalty and benefit—ending life only.
translations.idiomatic: Still my service aims only at your good—unto death.

sentences.zh: 若乃變心易慮，以偷榮取容，此臣所不能也。

translations.literal: If it should be changing heart and altering thought to steal glory and seek accommodation—this your servant cannot do.
translations.idiomatic: Ask me to trim sails for favor—I cannot.”

sentences.zh: "權辭謝焉。

translations.literal: " Quan apologized to him.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan apologized.

sentences.zh: 權以公孫淵稱藩，遣張彌、許晏至遼東拜淵為燕王。

translations.literal: Because Gongsun Yuan declared himself a vassal, Quan dispatched Zhang Mi and Xu Yan to Liaodong to invest Yuan as King of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: When Gongsun Yuan submitted as a client king, Sun Quan sent Zhang Mi and Xu Yan to Liaodong to enfeoff him as king of Yan.

sentences.zh: 昭諫曰："淵背魏懼討，遠來求援，非本志也。

translations.literal: Zhao remonstrated saying: "Yuan betrayed Wei and feared punitive attack—coming far to seek aid is not his original intent.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhao argued: “Yuan broke with Wei out of fear—that plea for help is opportunism, not conviction.

sentences.zh: 若淵改圖，欲自明於魏，兩使不反，不亦取笑於天下乎?"權與相反覆，昭意彌切。

translations.literal: If Yuan changes plan and wishes to clarify himself to Wei, both envoys not returning—is it not also inviting laughter from the realm?" Quan debated back and forth with him—Zhao's intent grew ever sharper.
translations.idiomatic: If he swings back to Wei, two dead envoys will make us the empire’s laughingstock.” Sun Quan argued harder; Zhang Zhao doubled down.

sentences.zh: 權不能堪，案刀而怒曰："吳國士人入宮則拜孤，出宮則拜君，孤之敬君，亦為至矣，而數於眾中折孤，孤嘗恐失計。

translations.literal: Quan could not endure it—pressed his sword and angrily said: "Wu gentlemen entering the palace bow to me—leaving the palace they bow to you—my reverence for you has likewise reached the utmost—yet you repeatedly humiliate me before the multitude—I constantly fear losing judgment.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan slammed his blade down: “Courtiers bow to me inside and to you outside—I honor you past measure—yet you shame me in public till I doubt myself.

sentences.zh: "昭熟視權曰："臣雖知言不用，每竭愚忠者，誠以太后臨崩，呼老臣於床下，遺詔顧命之言故在耳。

translations.literal: Zhao stared fixedly at Quan saying: "Although your servant knows his words are unused, each time he exhausts foolish loyalty—it is truly because when the Dowager faced death she called the old minister beneath the bed—the testament words of entrusting mandate still ring in the ears.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhao held his gaze: “I nag though you ignore me because Lady Wu’s deathbed charge still rings in my ears.

sentences.zh: "因涕泣橫流。

translations.literal: " Thereupon tears streamed horizontally.
translations.idiomatic: ” Tears streamed down his face.

sentences.zh: 權擲刀致地，與昭對泣。

translations.literal: Quan threw the sword to the ground and wept facing Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan dropped his sword and wept with Zhang Zhao.

sentences.zh: 然卒遣彌、晏往。

translations.literal: Yet in the end he dispatched Mi and Yan to go.
translations.idiomatic: Still he sent Zhang Mi and Xu Yan.

sentences.zh: 昭忿言之不用，稱疾不朝。

translations.literal: Zhao indignant that his words were not employed claimed illness and did not attend court.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhao boycotted court, feigning illness.

sentences.zh: 權恨之，土塞其門，昭又於內以土封之。

translations.literal: Quan resented it—earth blocked his gate—Zhao again on the inside sealed it with earth.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan piled earth against his door; Zhang Zhao walled himself in from within.

sentences.zh: 淵果殺彌，晏。

translations.literal: Yuan indeed killed Mi and Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Gongsun Yuan executed both envoys.

sentences.zh: 權數慰謝昭，昭固不起，權因出過其門呼昭，昭辭疾篤。

translations.literal: Quan repeatedly consoled and apologized to Zhao—Zhao stubbornly would not rise—Quan therefore went out passing his gate calling Zhao—Zhao declined grave illness.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan apologized again and again; Zhang Zhao stayed “sick”; when the sovereign called at his gate he pleaded mortal illness.

sentences.zh: 權燒其門，欲以恐之，昭更閉門戶。

translations.literal: Quan burned his gate wishing to frighten him—Zhao further closed door and windows.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan set fire to the gate to scare him—Zhang Zhao only barred his doors tighter.

sentences.zh: 權使人滅火，住門良久，昭諸子共扶昭起，權載以還宮，深自克責。

translations.literal: Quan had people extinguish the fire—stood long at the gate—Zhao's sons together helped Zhao rise—Quan carried him in a cart returning to the palace—deeply blaming himself.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan called off the blaze, waited at the door until Zhang Zhao’s sons carried him out, drove him to the palace, and scourged himself.

sentences.zh: 昭不得已，然後朝會。

translations.literal: Zhao had no choice—thereafter attended assembly.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhao yielded and returned to court.

sentences.zh: 〈习凿齿曰：张昭於是乎不臣矣！

translations.literal: Xi Zuochi states: Zhang Zhao here ceased being a minister!
translations.idiomatic: (Xi Zuochi: Zhang Zhao ceased behaving as a subject!)

sentences.zh: 夫臣人者，三谏不从则奉身而退，身苟不绝，何忿懟之有？

translations.literal: One who serves a man—if thrice remonstrated and not obeyed then withdraw body and retire—if the body is not cut off—what resentment can there be?
translations.idiomatic: A minister who is ignored thrice should resign alive—no cause for spite.

sentences.zh: 且秦穆违谏，卒霸西戎，晋文暂怒，终成大业。

translations.literal: Moreover Duke Mu of Qin disobeyed remonstrance yet ended hegemon of western Rong; Duke Wen of Jin briefly raged yet finally completed great enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Mu defied advice yet conquered the west; Duke Wen of Jin flared yet finished the work.

sentences.zh: 遗誓以悔过见录，狐偃无怨绝之辞，君臣道泰，上下俱荣。

translations.literal: Bequeathed oath took regret as recorded—Hu Yan had no words of resentful severance—lord and minister's way was smooth—above and below both glorious.
translations.idiomatic: Old oaths forgive slips—Hu Yan did not storm off—good rulers and ministers thrive together.

sentences.zh: 今权悔往之非而求昭，后益回虑降心，不远而复，是其善也。

translations.literal: Now Quan regretted past errors and sought Zhao—later turning thought further and lowering heart—not far yet returning—that is his goodness.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan admitted fault and humbled himself—that was virtue.

sentences.zh: 昭为人臣，不度权得道，匡其后失，夙夜匪懈，以延来誉，乃追忿不用，归罪於君，闭户拒命，坐待焚灭，岂不悖哉！〉

translations.literal: Zhao as man's minister—did not measure Quan obtaining the Way and correcting his later faults—diligent day and night without slack—to extend coming praise—yet pursued resentment at non-employment—returning blame to the lord—closing doors rejecting command—sitting awaiting burning extinction—is it not contrary!〉
translations.idiomatic: Yet Zhang Zhao as minister never measured whether Sun Quan had mended—he sulked, blamed his lord, and waited for the fire—mad conduct.)

sentences.zh: 昭容貌矜嚴，有威風，權常曰："孤與張公言，不敢妄也。

translations.literal: Zhao's appearance was stern and dignified with awe-inspiring presence—Quan constantly said: "I with Lord Zhang speak—I dare not speak rashly.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhao looked formidable; Sun Quan said: “With Zhang Gong I watch every word.

sentences.zh: "舉邦憚之。

translations.literal: " The whole state feared him.
translations.idiomatic: ” The whole court stood in awe.

sentences.zh: 年八十一，嘉禾五年卒。

translations.literal: At age eighty-one he died fifth year of Jiahe.
translations.idiomatic: He died at eighty-one in Jiahe 5.

sentences.zh: 遺令幅巾素棺，斂以時服。

translations.literal: His testament ordered cloth headwrap and plain coffin—buried in seasonal dress.
translations.idiomatic: He asked for a simple headcloth, plain coffin, and everyday clothes.

sentences.zh: 權素服臨吊，謚曰文侯。

translations.literal: Quan in plain garments attended mourning—posthumous title Marquis Wen.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan wore mourning and gave him the posthumous name Marquis Wen.

sentences.zh: 〈典略曰：余曩闻刘荆州尝自作书欲与孙伯符，以示祢正平，正平蚩之，言：“如是为欲使孙策帐下兒读之邪，将使张子布见乎？

translations.literal: Dian lüe states: Your servant formerly heard Inspector Liu of Jingzhou once himself composed a letter wishing to give to Sun Boji—showed it to Mi Zhengping—Zhengping sneered at it saying: "Like this—is it wanting children under Sun Ce's tent to read it, or wanting Zhang Zibu to see it?
translations.idiomatic: (The Dian lüe: Liu Biao once drafted a letter for Sun Ce and showed Mi Heng; Mi sneered—did Liu mean Sun Ce’s boys or Zhang Zhao to read it?

sentences.zh: ”如正平言，以为子布之才高乎？

translations.literal: " According to Zhengping's words—does one think Zibu's talent is higher?
translations.idiomatic: ” Did Mi mean Zhang Zhao outshone him?

sentences.zh: 虽然，犹自蕴藉典雅，不可谓之无笔迹也。

translations.literal: Although so—still self-contained and refined elegance—cannot be called without literary trace.
translations.idiomatic: Still the draft was polished—far from illiterate.

sentences.zh: 加闻吴中称谓之仲父，如此，其人信一时之良幹，恨其不於嵩岳等资，而乃播殖於会稽。〉

translations.literal: Moreover hearing Wu called him its Zhongfu—in this way that man was truly a fine pillar of the age—regretting he did not root on Mount Song but broadcast seed in Kuaiji.〉
translations.idiomatic: Wu dubbed Zhang Zhao its Guan Zhong—what a minister—yet Pei regrets he bloomed in the south, not the Central Plain.)

sentences.zh: 長子承已自封侯，少子休襲爵。

translations.literal: Eldest son Cheng had already been enfeoffed marquis—younger son Xiu inherited the noble rank.
translations.idiomatic: Eldest son Zhang Cheng already held a marquisate; younger Zhang Xiu inherited.

sentences.zh: 侄 奮

translations.literal: Nephew Fen
translations.idiomatic: Nephew Zhang Fen

sentences.zh: 昭弟子奮年二十，造作攻城大攻車，為步騭所薦。

translations.literal: Zhao's nephew Fen at age twenty constructed a great siege assault cart—recommended by Bu Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty Zhang Fen built a heavy siege engine on Bu Zhi’s recommendation.

sentences.zh: 昭不願曰："妝年尚少，何為自委於軍旅乎?"奮對曰："昔童汪死難，子奇治阿，奮實不才耳，於年不為少也。

translations.literal: Zhao unwilling said: "You are still young—why cast yourself into armies?" Fen replied saying: "Formerly child Wang died for duty—Ziqi ruled E—I Fen truly lack talent—in age it is not considered young.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhao protested: “You are too young for camp.” Zhang Fen cited boy-warriors and Ziqi of E— “Talent matters, not age.”

sentences.zh: "遂領兵為將軍，連有功效，至

translations.literal: " Thereupon he led troops as general—continuously had merit and results—reaching
translations.idiomatic: He took command, won repeated victories, and rose to

sentences.zh: （平州）

translations.literal: (Pingzhou)
translations.idiomatic: (Ping province)

sentences.zh: 都督，封樂鄉亭侯。

translations.literal: chief inspector—enfeoffed Village Marquis of Lexiang.
translations.idiomatic: inspector-in-chief with the village marquisate of Lexiang.

sentences.zh: 子 承

translations.literal: Son Cheng
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Cheng

sentences.zh: 承字仲嗣，少以才學知名，與諸葛瑾、步騭、嚴畯相友善。

translations.literal: Cheng, courtesy name Zhongsi—in youth by talent and learning became known—together with Zhuge Jin, Bu Zhi, and Yan Jun were mutually friendly.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Cheng, styled Zhongsi, famous young for scholarship; befriended Zhuge Jin, Bu Zhi, and Yan Jun.

sentences.zh: 權為驃騎將軍，辟西曹掾，出為長沙西部都尉。

translations.literal: When Quan was agile-cavalry general he summoned him western bureau aide—went out as western commandant of Changsha.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan as agile-cavalry general named him western bureau aide, then west commandant of Changsha.

sentences.zh: 討平山寇，得精兵萬五千人。

translations.literal: He campaigned and pacified mountain bandits—obtained fifteen thousand picked troops.
translations.idiomatic: He crushed hill bandits and raised fifteen thousand elite men.

sentences.zh: 後為濡須都督、奮威將軍，封都鄉侯，領部曲五千人。

translations.literal: Later became inspector of Ruxu and General Who Displays Might—enfeoffed Marquis of Dou Township—commanded five thousand troops of his command.
translations.idiomatic: Later he commanded Ruxu, became General Who Displays Might, marquis of Dou township, with five thousand household troops.

sentences.zh: 承為人壯毅忠讜，能甄識人物，拔彭城蔡款、南陽謝景於孤微童幼，後並為國士，款至衛尉，景豫章太守。

translations.literal: Cheng as a man was stalwart, loyal, and frank—able to discern men—raised Pengcheng Cai Kuan and Nanyang Xie Jing from obscure infancy—afterward both became gentlemen of the state—Kuan reached Commandant of the Guards—Jing Administrator of Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: Staunch and blunt, he spotted Cai Kuan and Xie Jing as boys in obscurity; both rose—Cai to commandant of the guards, Xie to Yuzhang prefect.

sentences.zh: 〈吴录曰：款字文德，历位内外，以清贞显於当世。

translations.literal: Wu lu states: Kuan's courtesy name Wende—passed through inner and outer posts—by purity and integrity displayed in the age.
translations.idiomatic: (The Wu lu: Cai Kuan, styled Wende, served everywhere and shone for integrity.)

sentences.zh: 后以卫尉领中书令，封留侯。

translations.literal: Later as Commandant of the Guards headed Imperial Secretariat Director—enfeoffed Marquis of Liu.
translations.idiomatic: He later combined commandant of the guards with palace secretary and received the marquisate of Liu.

sentences.zh: 二子，条、机。

translations.literal: Two sons—Tiao and Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Two sons: Cai Tiao and Cai Ji.

sentences.zh: 条孙皓时位至尚书令、太子少傅。

translations.literal: Tiao under Sun Hao reached Secretary Director and junior tutor to the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Tiao rose under Sun Hao to secretary director and junior tutor to the heir.

sentences.zh: 机为临川太守。

translations.literal: Ji was Administrator of Linchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Ji became Linchuan prefect.

sentences.zh: 谢景事在《孙登传》。〉

translations.literal: Xie Jing's affair is in Sun Deng's biography.〉
translations.idiomatic: Xie Jing’s story appears under Sun Deng.)

sentences.zh: 又諸葛恪年少時，眾人奇其英才。

translations.literal: Moreover when Zhuge Ke was young the multitude marveled at his hero talent.
translations.idiomatic: When young Zhuge Ke dazzled everyone.

sentences.zh: 承言終敗諸葛氏者，元遜也。

translations.literal: Cheng stated that in the end the one who would destroy the Zhuge clan was Yuansun.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Cheng predicted Zhuge Ke would ruin the Zhuge house.

sentences.zh: 勤於長進，篤於物類，凡在庶幾之流，無不造門，年六十七，赤烏七年卒，謚曰定侯。

translations.literal: Diligent in advancing—earnest toward things—in all who were of near-worthy class none failed to visit his gate—at age sixty-seven died seventh year of Chiwu—posthumous title Marquis Ding.
translations.idiomatic: He promoted talent tirelessly, visited every promising scholar, died at sixty-seven in Chiwu 7 with posthumous name Ding.

sentences.zh: 子震嗣。

translations.literal: His son Zhen succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Son Zhang Zhen inherited.

sentences.zh: 初，承喪妻，昭欲為索諸葛瑾女，承以相與有好，難之，權聞而勸焉，遂為婿。

translations.literal: At first when Cheng lost his wife Zhao wished to seek Zhuge Jin's daughter for him—Cheng because they were mutually friendly found it difficult—Quan heard and urged—thereupon became son-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Cheng was widowed, Zhang Zhao wanted Zhuge Jin’s daughter; Zhang Cheng hesitated because they were friends—Sun Quan urged the match.

sentences.zh: 〈臣松之案：承与诸葛瑾同以赤乌中卒，计承年小瑾四岁耳。〉

translations.literal: Your servant Songzhi investigates: Cheng together with Zhuge Jin both died in Chiwu period—reckoning Cheng's age four years younger than Jin only.〉
translations.idiomatic: (Pei Songzhi: Zhang Cheng and Zhuge Jin died the same years—Zhang Cheng only four years younger.)

sentences.zh: 生女，權為子和納之。

translations.literal: Bore a daughter—Quan for his son He took her in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Their daughter married Sun Quan’s son Sun He.

sentences.zh: 權數令和修敬於承，執子婿之禮。

translations.literal: Quan repeatedly ordered He to cultivate reverence toward Cheng—holding son-in-law ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan told Sun He to honor Zhang Cheng as his father-in-law.

sentences.zh: 震諸葛恪誅時亦死。

translations.literal: When Zhuge Ke was executed Zhen likewise died.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhen died when Zhuge Ke fell.

sentences.zh: 子 休

translations.literal: Son Xiu
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xiu

sentences.zh: 休字叔嗣，弱冠與諸葛恪、顧譚等俱為太子登僚友，以《漢書》授登。

translations.literal: Xiu, courtesy name Shusi—at capping age together with Zhuge Ke, Gu Tan and others all were companions and friends of the heir Deng—instructed Deng in the Han Records.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xiu, styled Shusi, joined Zhuge Ke and Gu Tan as companions to heir Sun Deng and taught him the Han Records.

sentences.zh: 〈吴书曰：休进授，指摘文义，分别事物，并有章条。

translations.literal: Wu shu states: Xiu advancing instruction picked apart literary meaning—divided things and affairs—and had chapter and clause.
translations.idiomatic: (The Wu shu: Zhang Xiu parsed texts into neat sections.)

sentences.zh: 每升堂宴饮，酒酣乐作，登辄降意与同欢乐。

translations.literal: Whenever ascending hall for banquet drinking—wine deep music rising—Deng always lowered intent to share joy with him.
translations.idiomatic: At banquets Sun Deng joined the music and drank with him.

sentences.zh: 休为人解达，登甚爱之，常在左右。〉

translations.literal: Xiu as a man was open and fluent—Deng greatly loved him—constantly at right and left.〉
translations.idiomatic: Sun Deng adored his frank wit and kept him close.)

sentences.zh: 從中庶子轉為右弼都尉。

translations.literal: From gentleman attendant of the heir transferred to right aide commandant.
translations.idiomatic: He moved from heir’s attendant to right aide commandant.

sentences.zh: 權常遊獵，迨幕乃歸，休上疏諫戒，權大善之，以示於昭。

translations.literal: Quan constantly hunted—until dusk then returned—Xiu submitted memorial remonstrating and warning—Quan greatly praised it—showed it to Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan hunted till dusk; Zhang Xiu remonstrated; Sun Quan praised him and showed Zhang Zhao.

sentences.zh: 及登卒後，為侍中，拜羽林都督，平三典軍事，遷揚武將軍。

translations.literal: When after Deng died he became attendant-in-ordinary—invested Colonel Commandant of the Feathered Forest—directed the three military bureaus—promoted General Who Displays Might.
translations.idiomatic: After Sun Deng died he rose to attendant-in-chief, colonel of the Feathered Forest, overseer of three military offices, then General Who Displays Might.

sentences.zh: 為魯王霸友黨所譖，與顧譚、承俱以芍陂論功事，休、承與典軍陳恂通情，詐增其伐，並徙交州。

translations.literal: Slandered by Prince Lu Ba's friendly faction—together with Gu Tan and Cheng all because of Shao Lake merit debate affair—Xiu, Cheng together with military recorder Chen Xun communicated feelings—falsely augmented his merit—all banished to Jiao Province.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Lu’s clique framed him with Gu Tan and Gu Cheng over credit for Shao Lake—he and Gu Cheng colluded with Chen Xun to pad the tally—and all were exiled to Jiao.

sentences.zh: 中書令孫弘佞偽險詖，休素所忿，

translations.literal: Secretariat Director Sun Hong was servile, false, treacherous, and crooked—Xiu always resented him
translations.idiomatic: The flatterer Sun Hong angered Zhang Xiu

sentences.zh: 〈吴录云：弘，会稽人也。〉

translations.literal: Wu lu states: Hong was a man of Kuaiji.〉
translations.idiomatic: (The Wu lu: Sun Hong came from Kuaiji.)

sentences.zh: 弘因是譖訴，下詔書賜休死，時年四十一。

translations.literal: Hong exploited this to slander and complain—edict was issued bestowing Xiu death—at the time age forty-one.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Hong denounced him; an edict forced Zhang Xiu to die at forty-one.

sentences.zh: 顧雍字元歎，吳郡吳人也。

translations.literal: Gu Yong, courtesy name Yutan—a man of Wu in Wu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Yong, styled Yutan, from Wu commandery.

sentences.zh: 〈吴录曰：雍曾祖父奉，字季鸿，颍川太守。〉

translations.literal: Wu lu states: Yong's great-grandfather Feng, courtesy name Jihong—Administrator of Yingchuan.〉
translations.idiomatic: (The Wu lu: great-grandfather Gu Feng, styled Jihong, was Yingchuan prefect.)

sentences.zh: 蔡伯喈從朔方還，嘗避怨於吳，雍從學琴書。

translations.literal: Cai Yong returned from Shuofang—once avoided resentment in Wu—Yong followed him studying zither and writing.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Yong fled to Wu from Shuofang; Gu Yong studied music and calligraphy under him.

sentences.zh: 〈江表传曰：雍从伯喈学，专一清静，敏而易教。

translations.literal: Jiangbiao zhuan states: Yong followed Bojie to study—single-minded quiet purity—keen and easy to teach.
translations.idiomatic: (The Jiangbiao zhuan: Gu Yong studied with Cai Yong—quiet, sharp, teachable.)

sentences.zh: 伯喈贵异之，谓曰：「卿必成致，今以吾名与卿。

translations.literal: Bojie prized him as unusual—said to him: "You will surely achieve completion—now I give my name to you.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Yong said: “You will accomplish much—I lend you my given name.

sentences.zh: 」故雍与伯喈同名，由此也。

translations.literal: " Therefore Yong shares Bojie's name—because of this.
translations.idiomatic: ” Hence Gu Yong shares Cai Yong’s name.

sentences.zh: 吴录曰：雍字元叹，言为蔡雍之所叹，因以为字焉。〉

translations.literal: Wu lu states: Yong's character Yutan—meaning praised by Cai Yong—therefore took it as courtesy name.〉
translations.idiomatic: (The Wu lu: “Yutan” means “the one Cai Yong praised.”)

sentences.zh: 州郡表薦，弱冠為合肥長，後轉在婁、曲阿、上虞，皆有治跡。

translations.literal: Commandery and prefecture memorialized recommendation—at capping age became chief of Hefei—later transferred at Lou, Qu’e, and Shangyu—all had traces of good rule.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended young, he served Hefei, then Lou, Qu’e, and Shangyu with a fine record.

sentences.zh: 孫權領會稽太守，不之郡，以雍為丞，行太守事，討除寇賊，郡界寧靜，吏民歸服，數年，入為左司馬。

translations.literal: Sun Quan held concurrent Administrator of Kuaiji—did not go to the commandery—appointed Yong assistant—acting Administrator affairs—suppressed and eliminated bandits—commandery boundary peaceful—clerks and people submitted—in several years entered as left marshal.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan held Kuaiji in title; Gu Yong ran it as aide, crushed bandits, won the people, then entered as left marshal.

sentences.zh: 權為吳王，累遷大理、奉常，領尚書令，封陽遂鄉侯，拜侯還寺，而家人不知，後聞乃驚。

translations.literal: When Quan became King of Wu—accumulated promotions to grand judge and minister of ceremonies—heading Secretariat Director—enfeoffed Township Marquis of Yangsui—on returning from investiture family members did not know—later hearing were astonished.
translations.idiomatic: As king of Wu Gu Yong rose to grand judge, minister of ceremonies, and secretary director, marquis of Yangsui—his household learned only when he came home enfeoffed.

sentences.zh: 黃武四年，迎母於吳。

translations.literal: Huangwu fourth year welcomed mother at Wu.
translations.idiomatic: In Huangwu 4 he brought his mother to Wu.

sentences.zh: 既至，權臨賀之，親拜其母於庭，公卿大臣畢會，後太子又往慶焉。

translations.literal: When she arrived Quan came to congratulate—personally bowed to his mother in the courtyard—dukes and great ministers all assembled—afterward the heir again went to celebrate.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan greeted her, bowed to Lady Gu in court, filled the hall with lords, and sent the heir to honor her.

sentences.zh: 雍為人不飲酒，寡言語，舉動時當。

translations.literal: Yong as a man did not drink wine—spoke few words—movements timely and appropriate.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Yong drank nothing, spoke little, moved with quiet propriety.

sentences.zh: 權嘗歎曰：「顧君不言，言必有中。

translations.literal: Quan once sighed saying: "Lord Gu without speaking—when he speaks must hit the mark.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan said: “When Gu Yong speaks, he hits the mark.

sentences.zh: 」至飲宴歡樂之際，左右恐有酒失而雍必見之，是以不敢肆情。

translations.literal: " At drinking banquet joyous pleasure occasions—left and right feared there might be wine faults yet Yong must see them—therefore did not dare indulge feelings.
translations.idiomatic: ” At feasts attendants feared Gu Yong’s gaze and checked their cups.

sentences.zh: 權亦曰：「顧公在坐，使人不樂。

translations.literal: Quan also said: "With Lord Duke seated—it makes people unhappy.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan joked: “Gu Yong kills the mood.

sentences.zh: 」其見憚如此。

translations.literal: " He was feared thus.
translations.idiomatic: ” Everyone feared him.

sentences.zh: 是歲，改為太常。

translations.literal: That year changed to Minister of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: That year he became minister of ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 進封醴陵侯，代孫邵為丞相，平尚書事。

translations.literal: Advanced enfeoffment Marquis of Liling—replacing Sun Shao as chancellor—balancing Secretariat affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to marquis of Liling, he succeeded Sun Shao as chancellor over the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 其所選用文武將吏各隨能所任，心無適莫。

translations.literal: Those he selected and employed civil and military generals and clerks each followed ability and appointment—heart without preference or rejection.
translations.idiomatic: He placed civil and military men strictly on merit without favoritism.

sentences.zh: 時訪逮民間，及政職所宜，輒密以聞。

translations.literal: At times visiting and pursuing among the people—and administrative duties what was fitting—always secretly reported.
translations.idiomatic: He toured the folkways and whispered policy notes to the throne.

sentences.zh: 若見納用，則歸之於上，不用，終不宣洩。

translations.literal: If seen and adopted used—then attributed to superiors—if not used—ultimately did not divulge.
translations.idiomatic: If Sun Quan acted on his tip, Gu Yong credited the ruler; if ignored, he stayed silent.

sentences.zh: 權以此重之，然於公朝有所陳及，辭色雖順而所執者正。

translations.literal: Quan therefore esteemed him—yet at public court what he presented and reached—though compliant in wording and color—what he grasped was correct.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan valued his discretion; in council Gu Yong spoke softly but held firm.

sentences.zh: 權嘗咨問得失，張昭因陳聽采聞，頗以法令太稠，刑罰微重，宜有所蠲損。

translations.literal: Quan once consulted asking gains and losses—Zhang Zhao therefore presented listening collection hearsay—rather holding laws and orders too dense—punishments slightly heavy—ought to have something reduced and cut.
translations.idiomatic: Once Sun Quan asked for counsel; Zhang Zhao said laws were thick and penalties harsh.

sentences.zh: 權默然，顧問雍曰：「君以為何如？

translations.literal: Quan silent—turned asking Yong saying: "Lord—what do you think?
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan turned to Gu Yong: “Your view?”

sentences.zh: 」雍對曰：「臣之所聞，亦如昭所陳。

translations.literal: " Yong replied saying: "What your servant has heard—likewise like Zhao presented.
translations.idiomatic: ” Gu Yong said: “I agree with Zhang Zhao.

sentences.zh: 」於是權乃議獄輕刑。

translations.literal: " Thereupon Quan discussed prisons lightening punishments.
translations.idiomatic: ” Sun Quan relaxed criminal law.

sentences.zh: 〈江表传曰：灌常令中书郎诣雍，有所咨访。

translations.literal: Jiangbiao zhuan states: Quan constantly ordered Secretariat Gentleman to visit Yong—having matters to consult and inquire.
translations.idiomatic: (The Jiangbiao zhuan: Sun Quan sent secretariat clerks to consult Gu Yong.)

sentences.zh: 若合雍意，事可施行，即与相反覆，究而论之，为设酒食。

translations.literal: If matching Yong's intent—affairs could be enacted—then with him debated back and forth—investigating and discussing—for him set wine and food.
translations.idiomatic: If the clerk’s plan matched Gu Yong’s, they refined it over dinner.)

sentences.zh: 如不合意，雍即正色改容，默然不言，无所施设，即退告。

translations.literal: If it did not match intent—Yong immediately with stern color changed countenance—silent without speaking—applied nothing—thereupon withdrew and reported.
translations.idiomatic: If Gu Yong disagreed, his face went cold; he said nothing, offered nothing, withdrew, and reported.

sentences.zh: 权曰：「顾公欢悦，是事合宜也；

translations.literal: Quan said: "Lord Gu cheerful—that means the affair fits."
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan said: "If Gu Yong smiles, the plan is sound."

sentences.zh: 其不言者，是事未平也，孤当重思之。

translations.literal: That he does not speak means the affair is not settled—I ought rethink it.
translations.idiomatic: When he stays silent, the matter is still wrong—I must think again.

sentences.zh: 」其见敬信如此。

translations.literal: " He was revered and trusted thus.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the trust he commanded.

sentences.zh: 江边诸将，各欲立功自效，多陈便宜，有所掩袭。

translations.literal: The various generals along the river each wished to establish merit and prove themselves—many presented convenient proposals—having matters of surprise raid.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier generals pitched raids for glory.

sentences.zh: 权以访雍，雍曰：「臣闻兵法戒於小利，此等所陈，欲邀功名而为其身，非为国也，陛下宜禁制。

translations.literal: Quan consulted Yong—Yong said: "Your servant has heard military arts warn against petty profit—these presentations wish to invite merit and fame for themselves—not for the state—Your Majesty ought forbid them.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan asked Gu Yong, who said: "The Art of War warns against petty gains—these men chase credit, not the realm—stop them."

sentences.zh: 苟不足以曜威损敌，所不宜听也。

translations.literal: If insufficient to display majesty and harm the enemy—it is not fitting to listen.
translations.idiomatic: Unless a strike truly hurts the foe, ignore it.

sentences.zh: 」权从之。

translations.literal: " Quan followed him.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan agreed.

sentences.zh: 军国得失，行事可不，自非面见，口未尝言之。〉

translations.literal: Army and state gains and losses—conduct feasible or not—unless face-to-face meeting—mouth never spoke them.〉
translations.idiomatic: He never spoke policy aloud except face-to-face.)

sentences.zh: 久之，呂壹、秦博為中書，典校諸官府及州郡文書。

translations.literal: After long—Lu Yi and Qin Bo became Secretariat—investigating and comparing documents of all official bureaus and prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yi and Qin Bo ran the palace secretariat and audited every office.

sentences.zh: 壹等因此漸作威福，遂造作榷酤障管之利，舉罪糾奸，纖介必聞，重以深案丑誣，毀短大臣，排陷無辜，雍等皆見舉白，用被譴讓。

translations.literal: Yi and cohort exploited this gradually making awe and blessing—thereupon fabricating monopoly ale barrier-guard profits—raising crimes investigating wickedness—fine hair must be heard—heavy with deep case ugly slander—destroying and shortening great ministers—framing and trapping the innocent—Yong and cohort all were reported white—thereby receiving blame and reproof.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yi abused the audit to tax salt and wine, hunt petty guilt, slander chiefs, and shame Gu Yong until ministers were censured.

sentences.zh: 後壹奸罪發露，收系延尉。

translations.literal: Later Yi's wicked crimes issued forth exposed—arrested and bound at Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: When Lu Yi's crimes surfaced, the court jailed him.

sentences.zh: 雍往斷獄。

translations.literal: Yong went to judge the prison.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Yong tried the case.

sentences.zh: 壹以囚見，雍和顏色，問其辭狀，臨出，又謂壹曰：「君意得無慾有所道？

translations.literal: Yi as prisoner met—Yong with harmonious countenance asked his plea statement—at departure—again said to Yi: "Lord—could it be you wish to say something?
translations.idiomatic: He questioned Lu Yi gently and asked before leaving whether he had more to say.

sentences.zh: 」壹叩頭無言。

translations.literal: " Yi knocked head without words.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yi kowtowed in silence.

sentences.zh: 時尚書郎懷敘面詈辱壹，雍責敘曰：「官有正法，何至於此？」

translations.literal: At that time Secretariat Gentleman Huai Xu reviled Yi to his face—Yong reproved Xu saying: "Officials have correct law—how reach this?"
translations.idiomatic: Secretariat clerk Huai Xu cursed Lu Yi; Gu Yong scolded him: "We have laws—no street abuse."

sentences.zh: 〈江表传曰：权嫁从女，女顾氏甥，故请雍父子及孙谭，谭时为选曹尚书，见任贵重。

translations.literal: Jiangbiao zhuan states: Quan married a collateral daughter—daughter was Gu clan niece—therefore invited Yong father and sons and Sun Tan—Tan at that time was Selection Bureau Secretary—seen as entrusted weighty.
translations.idiomatic: (The Jiangbiao zhuan: Sun Quan wed a niece to the Gus and invited Gu Yong and Sun Tan—then chief of personnel.)

sentences.zh: 是日，权极欢。

translations.literal: That day Quan extremely joyous.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan reveled that night.

sentences.zh: 谭醉酒，三起舞，舞不知止。

translations.literal: Tan drunk with wine—thrice rose to dance—dance did not know to stop.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Tan danced drunk and would not stop.

sentences.zh: 雍内怒之。

translations.literal: Yong inwardly angered at him.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Yong seethed.

sentences.zh: 明日，召谭，诃责之曰：「君王以含垢为德，臣下以恭谨为节。

translations.literal: Next day summoned Tan—scolded him saying: "The ruler king takes bearing shame as virtue—subordinates take respectful caution as norm.
translations.idiomatic: Next day he rebuked Sun Tan: "Rulers endure slights; ministers stay humble."

sentences.zh: 昔萧何、吴汉并有大功，何每见高帝，似不能言；

translations.literal: Formerly Xiao He and Wu Han both had great merit—He whenever saw Gaodi seemed unable to speak;
translations.idiomatic: Xiao He froze before Gaozu;

sentences.zh: 汉奉光武，亦信恪勤。

translations.literal: Han served Guangwu—also trusted diligent earnestness.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Han served Guangwu with sober zeal.

sentences.zh: 汝之於国，宁有汗马之劳，可书之事邪？

translations.literal: You toward the state—how have sweat-blood horse toil—matters worth recording?
translations.idiomatic: What great deeds have you for Wu?

sentences.zh: 但阶门户之资，遂见宠任耳，何有舞不复知止？

translations.literal: Only step on gate-and-portal capital—thereupon seen favored and entrusted—how have dancing not again know stop?
translations.idiomatic: You ride family rank—how dare you dance on like a fool?

sentences.zh: 虽为酒后，亦由恃恩忘敬，谦虚不足。

translations.literal: Although because after wine—also by relying on grace forgetting reverence—modesty insufficient.
translations.idiomatic: Drunk or not, you forgot respect.

sentences.zh: 损吾家者必尔也。

translations.literal: He who harms my house must be you.
translations.idiomatic: You will ruin our house.

sentences.zh: 」因背向壁卧，谭立过一时，乃见遣。

translations.literal: " Thereupon turned back facing wall lying—Tan stood past one watch—then was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: He turned to the wall; Sun Tan stood an hour before dismissal.

sentences.zh: 徐众评曰：雍不以吕壹见毁之故，而和颜悦色，诚长者矣。

translations.literal: Xu Zhong commented saying: Yong because Yi saw destruction's cause—not harmonious happy face—truly elder worthy.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Zhong: Gu Yong stayed kind to Lu Yi despite past slanders—a true elder.

sentences.zh: 然开引其意，问所欲道，此非也。

translations.literal: Yet opening and drawing his intent—asking what he wished to say—this was not right.
translations.idiomatic: Yet inviting Lu Yi's last words was wrong.

sentences.zh: 壹奸险乱法，毁伤忠贤，吴国寒心，自太子登、陆逊已下，切谏不能得，是以潘濬欲因会手剑之，以除国患，疾恶忠主，义形於色，而今乃发起令言。

translations.literal: Yi treacherous wicked disturbing law—destroying and harming loyal worthies—Wu state chilled heart—from heir Deng and Lu Xun downward—urgent remonstrance could not obtain—therefore Pan Jun wished at meeting to hand sword him—to remove state calamity—hating evil loyal lord—righteousness showing in face—yet now inaugurating letting speak.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yi wrecked loyal men; from Sun Deng and Lu Xun down everyone begged his death—Pan Jun meant to stab him at court—yet Gu Yong coaxed his confession.

sentences.zh: 若壹称枉邪，不申理，则非录狱本旨；

translations.literal: If Yi claimed injustice yet did not extend principle—then not recording prison original intent;
translations.idiomatic: If Lu Yi pleaded innocence without proof, the trial failed.

sentences.zh: 若承辞而奏之，吴主傥以敬丞相所言，而复原宥，伯言、承明不当悲慨哉！

translations.literal: If accepting speech and memorializing it—Wu ruler perhaps respecting what chief minister spoke—and restoring forgiveness—would Boyan and Chengming not deserve grief and indignation!
translations.idiomatic: If Sun Quan spared Lu Yi on Gu Yong's word, Lu Xun and Sun Deng would rage.

sentences.zh: 怀叙本无私恨，无所为嫌，故詈辱之，疾恶意耳，恶不仁者，其为仁也。

translations.literal: Huai Xu originally lacked private hatred—nothing by which to suspect—therefore reviled him—hating evil intent—hating not humane ones—that is humane.
translations.idiomatic: Huai Xu bore Lu Yi no grudge—he cursed out justice.

sentences.zh: 季武子死，曾点倚其门而歌；

translations.literal: When Jiwuzi died—Zeng Dian leaned on his gate and sang;
translations.idiomatic: When Jiwuzi died, Zeng Dian sang at his gate.

sentences.zh: 子晳创发，子产催令自裁。

translations.literal: Zi Xi cut hair—Zi Chan urged ordering self-execution.
translations.idiomatic: Zi Xi cut his hair; Zi Chan ordered suicide.

sentences.zh: 以此言之，雍不当责怀叙也。〉

translations.literal: Judging by this—Yong ought not reprove Huai Xu.〉
translations.idiomatic: So Gu Yong should not have scolded Huai Xu.)

sentences.zh: 雍為相十九年，年七十六，赤烏六年卒。

translations.literal: Yong was chancellor nineteen years—age seventy-six—died sixth year of Chiwu.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Yong served nineteen years as chancellor and died at seventy-six in Chiwu 6.

sentences.zh: 初疾微時，權令醫趙泉視之。

translations.literal: When first illness slight—Quan ordered physician Zhao Quan to examine him.
translations.idiomatic: Early in his illness Sun Quan sent Physician Zhao Quan.

sentences.zh: 拜其少子濟為騎都尉。

translations.literal: Invested his youngest son Ji as Chief of Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He promoted youngest son Gu Ji as chief of cavalry.

sentences.zh: 雍聞，悲曰：「泉善別生死，吾必不起，故上欲及吾目見濟拜也。

translations.literal: Yong hearing—grieved saying: "Quan is good at distinguishing life and death—I surely cannot rise—therefore superior wishes while my eyes still see Ji invested."
translations.idiomatic: Gu Yong said: "Zhao Quan reads life and death—I will die—so the sovereign promotes Ji while I can see."

sentences.zh: 」權素服臨吊，謚曰肅侯。

translations.literal: " Quan in plain garments attended mourning—posthumous title Marquis Su.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan mourned in plain dress and named him Marquis Su.

sentences.zh: 長子邵早卒，次子裕有篤疾，少子濟嗣，無後，絕。

translations.literal: Eldest son Shao died early—second son Yu had grave illness—youngest son Ji succeeded—without heir—cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Eldest Gu Shao died young; second Gu Yu was chronically ill; Gu Ji inherited but left no sons—the line ended.

sentences.zh: 永安元年，詔曰：「故丞相雍，至德忠賢，輔國以禮，而侯統廢絕。

translations.literal: Yong'an first year edict stated: "Former chancellor Yong—ultimate virtue loyal worthy—aided state with ritual—yet marquis lineage ended.
translations.idiomatic: In Yong'an 1 Sun Hao decreed Gu Yong's marquisate extinct.

sentences.zh: 朕甚愍之。

translations.literal: We greatly pity it.
translations.idiomatic: The throne mourned.

sentences.zh: 其以雍次子裕襲爵為醴陵候，以明著舊勳。」

translations.literal: Let Yong's second son Yu inherit noble rank as Marquis of Liling—to clearly display old merit."
translations.idiomatic: Gu Yu inherited the Liling marquisate to honor Gu Yong.

sentences.zh: 〈吴录曰：裕一名穆，终宜都太守。

translations.literal: Wu lu states: Yu alternate name Mu—ended Administrator of Yidu.〉
translations.idiomatic: (The Wu lu: Gu Yu, alias Mu, died as Yidu prefect.)

sentences.zh: 裕子荣。

translations.literal: Yu's son Rong.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Gu Rong.

sentences.zh: 晋书曰：荣字彦先，为东南名士，仕吴为黄门郎，在晋历显位。

translations.literal: Jin shu states: Rong courtesy name Yanxian—was southeast famed gentleman—served Wu as Gentleman of Yellow Gates—in Jin passed prominent posts.
translations.idiomatic: (The Jin shu: Gu Rong, styled Yanxian, famed in the southeast; Yellow Gates under Wu, high Jin offices.)

sentences.zh: 元帝初镇江东，以荣为军司马，礼遇甚重。

translations.literal: When Yuan Emperor first garrisoned Jiangdong—made Rong army marshal—ritual treatment very heavy.
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Rui secured Jiangdong he named Gu Rong army marshal with great honor.

sentences.zh: 卒，表赠侍中、骠骑将军、仪同三司。

translations.literal: Died—memorial invested attendant-in-chief—agile-cavalry general—ceremonies equal Three Offices.
translations.idiomatic: Dead, he won posthumous attendant-in-chief, agile cavalry, Three Ducal honors.

sentences.zh: 荣兄子禺，字孟著，少有名望，为散骑侍郎，早卒。

translations.literal: Rong's elder brother's son Yu—courtesy name Mengzhu—young had fame—was scattered-cavalry attendant—died early.
translations.idiomatic: Nephew Gu Yu, styled Mengzhu, was a rising Jin officer who died young.

sentences.zh: 吴书曰：雍母弟徽。

translations.literal: Wu shu states: Yong's younger brother by same mother Hui.
translations.idiomatic: (The Wu shu: younger brother Gu Hui.)

sentences.zh: 字子叹，少游学，有脣吻。

translations.literal: Courtesy name Zitan—young traveled studied—had eloquent lips.
translations.idiomatic: Styled Zitan, learned abroad, silver-tongued.

sentences.zh: 孙权统事，闻徽有才辩，召署主簿。

translations.literal: When Sun Quan assumed affairs—heard Hui had talent and debate—summoned and appointed chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan heard his rhetoric and made him chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 尝近出行，见营军将一男子至巿行刑，问之何罪，云盗百钱，徽语使住。

translations.literal: Once went out nearby—saw camp army leading one man to market carrying out punishment—asked what crime—said stole hundred cash—Hui spoke ordering halt.
translations.idiomatic: Once he stopped a hanging over one hundred cash.

sentences.zh: 须臾，驰诣阙陈启：「方今畜养士众以图北虏，视此兵丁壮健兒，且所盗少，愚乞哀原。

translations.literal: Shortly galloped to palace gate stating petition: "Now raising and nurturing scholar hosts to plan northern prisoners—view this soldier stalwart healthy lad—and what he stole little—I foolishly beg mercy forgive.
translations.idiomatic: He raced to court: "We need soldiers against Wei—spare this strong thief over pennies."

sentences.zh: ”权许而嘉之。

translations.literal: " Quan permitted and praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan agreed.

sentences.zh: 转东曹掾。

translations.literal: Transferred eastern bureau aide.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to eastern bureau aide.

sentences.zh: 或传曹公欲东，权谓徽曰：「卿孤腹心，今传孟德怀异意，莫足使揣之，卿为吾行。

translations.literal: Someone transmitted Duke Cao wished east—Quan said to Hui: "You are my belly heart—now rumor Mengde harbors different intent—not worth sending to probe—You go for me.
translations.idiomatic: Rumors said Cao Cao would march east; Sun Quan sent Gu Hui: "Learn his mind."

sentences.zh: 」拜辅义都尉，到北与曹公相见。

translations.literal: " Invested aide who aids righteousness—arrived north meeting Duke Cao.
translations.idiomatic: Named aide who aids righteousness; he met Cao Cao.

sentences.zh: 公具问境内消息，徽应对婉顺，因说江东大丰，山薮宿恶，皆慕化为善，义出作兵。

translations.literal: Duke fully asked inner territory news—Hui answered yielding smooth—thereupon saying Jiangdong great harvest—mountain marsh long wicked—all admired transformation becoming good—righteousness out making soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao asked after Wu; Gu Hui said harvests were rich and bandits had yielded.

sentences.zh: 公笑曰：「孤与孙将军一结婚姻，共辅汉室，义如一家，君何为道此？

translations.literal: Duke laughed saying: "I with General Sun one tied marriage—together assist Han house—righteousness like one family—why do you speak this?
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao laughed: "Sun Quan and I are kin—we aid the Han—why spin yarns?"

sentences.zh: 」徽曰：「正以明公与主将义固磐石，休戚共之，必欲知江表消息，是以及耳。

translations.literal: " Hui said: "Precisely because enlightened duke and chief general righteousness firm as stone—shared joy and sorrow—must wish to know Jiangbiao news—therefore reached ear.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Hui answered: "You are family—I report southland news."

sentences.zh: 」公厚待遣还。

translations.literal: " Duke treated generously sending back.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao treated him well and sent him home.

sentences.zh: 权问定云何，徽曰：「敌国隐情，卒难探察。

translations.literal: Quan asked settled how—Hui said: "Enemy state hidden situation—suddenly hard probe inspect.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan asked what he learned; Gu Hui said spying was hard.

sentences.zh: 然徽潜采听，方与袁谭交争，未有他意。

translations.literal: Yet Hui secretly gathered listening—just then with Yuan Tan mutually disputing—had no other intent.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he heard Cao Cao was busy fighting Yuan Tan.

sentences.zh: 」乃拜徽巴东太守，欲大用之，会卒。

translations.literal: " Thereupon invested Hui Administrator of Badong—wished greatly employ him—happened to die.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan named him Badong prefect but he died first.

sentences.zh: 子裕，字季则，少知名，位至镇东将军。

translations.literal: Son Yu—courtesy name Jize—young became known—rank reached General Who Guards the East.
translations.idiomatic: Son Gu Yu, styled Jize, rose to General Who Guards the East.

sentences.zh: 雍族人悌，字子通，以孝悌廉正闻於乡党。

translations.literal: Clansman Ti—courtesy name Zitong—by filial piety brother respect honesty integrity heard in village and hamlet.
translations.idiomatic: Kinsman Gu Ti, styled Zitong, famed for filial honor.

sentences.zh: 年十五为郡吏，除郎中，稍迁偏将军。

translations.literal: Age fifteen became commandery clerk—removed Gentleman of the Palace—gradually promoted partial general.
translations.idiomatic: County clerk at fifteen, gentleman of the palace, then partial general.

sentences.zh: 权末年，嫡庶不分，悌数与骠骑将军硃据共陈祸福，言辞切直，朝廷惮之。

translations.literal: Quan's late years—legitimate and illegitimate not distinguished—Ti repeatedly with agile-cavalry general Zhu Ju together stated fortune and disaster—words sharp straight—court feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Sun Quan's reign he and Zhu Ju warned bluntly about the succession.

sentences.zh: 待妻有礼，常夜入晨出，希见其面。

translations.literal: Treating wife with ritual—constantly entered night exited dawn—rarely saw her face.
translations.idiomatic: He visited his wife only nights—almost never saw her by day.

sentences.zh: 尝疾笃，妻出省之，悌命左右扶起，冠帻加袭，起对，趣令妻还，其贞洁不渎如此。

translations.literal: Once gravely ill—wife went out to visit—Ti ordered attendants raise him—cap and kerchief plus layered robes—rose to answer—urged ordering wife return—his chastity undefiled thus.
translations.idiomatic: Even sick he dressed fully when his wife visited—pure ritual.

sentences.zh: 悌父向历四县令，年老致仕，悌每得父书，常洒扫，整衣服，更设几筵，舒书其上，拜跪读之，每句应诺，毕，复再拜。

translations.literal: Ti's father Xiang passed four county magistracies—old age retired—Ti whenever obtained father's letter—always sprinkled swept—straightened clothes—again set table mat—spread letter atop—knelt reading—each phrase answered yes—finished—again twice bowed.
translations.idiomatic: His father served four counties; Gu Ti swept the room, dressed up, and knelt to read each letter.

sentences.zh: 若父有疾耗之问至，则临书垂涕，声语哽咽。

translations.literal: If father had illness news arriving—then faced letter dropping tears—voice words choked.
translations.idiomatic: Ill news brought tears mid-read.

sentences.zh: 父以寿终，悌饮浆不入口五日。

translations.literal: Father by longevity ended—Ti drank broth not entering mouth five days.
translations.idiomatic: He fasted five days when his father died.

sentences.zh: 权为作布衣一袭，皆摩絮著之，强令悌释服。

translations.literal: Quan for him made plain cloth single garment—all rubbed stuffing attached—forced ordered Ti release mourning garment.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan gave him padded coats and forced him out of deepest mourning.

sentences.zh: 悌虽以公议自割，犹以不见父丧，常画壁作棺柩象，设神座於下，每对之哭泣，服未阕而卒。

translations.literal: Ti although by public discussion self-cut—still because not seeing father's funeral—constantly painted wall making coffin image—set spirit seat below—each facing it weeping—mourning not ended yet died.
translations.idiomatic: Though public duty cut mourning short, he painted a coffin on his wall and wept till he died unfinished.

sentences.zh: 悌四子：彦、礼、谦、祕。

translations.literal: Ti four sons: Yan, Li, Qian, Mi.
translations.idiomatic: Four sons: Yan, Li, Qian, Mi.

sentences.zh: 秘，晋交州刺史。

translations.literal: Mi—Jin Administrator of Jiao Province.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Mi became Jin prefect of Jiao.

sentences.zh: 祕子众，尚书仆射。〉

translations.literal: Mi's son Zhong—Secretary Vice Director.〉
translations.idiomatic: Gu Mi's son Zhong rose to vice secretary.)

sentences.zh: 子 邵

translations.literal: Son Shao
translations.idiomatic: Gu Shao

sentences.zh: 邵字孝則，博覽書傳，好樂人倫。

translations.literal: Shao courtesy name Xiaze—read widely books and transmissions—loved delighting in human relations.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Shao, styled Xiaze, read widely and loved ethics.

sentences.zh: 少與舅陸績齊名，而陸遜、張敦、卜靜等皆亞焉。

translations.literal: Young together with maternal uncle Lu Ji equally famed—yet Lu Xun, Zhang Dun, Bu Jing and others all ranked below.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he rivaled uncle Lu Ji; Lu Xun, Zhang Dun, and Bu Jing stood slightly below.

sentences.zh: 〈吴录曰：敦字叔方，静字玄风，并吴郡人。

translations.literal: Wu lu states: Dun courtesy name Shufang—Jing courtesy name Xuanfeng—both men of Wu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: (The Wu lu: Zhang Dun styled Shufang; Bu Jing styled Xuanfeng—both from Wu.)

sentences.zh: 敦德量渊懿，清虚淡泊，又善文辞。

translations.literal: Dun's virtue capacity deep profound—pure empty bland pale—also skilled literary phrasing.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Dun was deep, quiet, and literary.

sentences.zh: 孙权为车骑将军，辟西曹掾，转主簿，出补海昬令，甚有惠化，年三十二卒。

translations.literal: Sun Quan was chariots-and-cavalry general—summoned western bureau aide—transferred chief clerk—went out supplementing Haihun magistrate—had very benevolent transformation—age thirty-two died.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan named him aide and Haihun magistrate; he died at thirty-two.

sentences.zh: 卜静终於剡令。〉

translations.literal: Bu Jing ended at Yan magistrate.〉
translations.idiomatic: Bu Jing died as magistrate of Yan.)

sentences.zh: 自州郡庶幾及四方人士，往來相見，或言議而去，或結厚而別，風聲流聞，遠近稱之。
