translations.literal: From commandery near-worthy and four quarters gentlemen—coming going mutually seeing—some spoke deliberation then left—some tied thick then parted—wind sound flowing heard—far and near praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars everywhere sought him out and praised his name.

sentences.zh: 權妻以策女。

translations.literal: Quan married him to Ce's daughter.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan married him to Sun Ce's daughter.

sentences.zh: 年二十七，起家為豫章太守。

translations.literal: Age twenty-seven—rose from house as Administrator of Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty-seven he became Yuzhang prefect.

sentences.zh: 下車祀先賢徐孺子之墓。

translations.literal: Descending cart sacrificed to former worthy Xu Ruzi's tomb.
translations.idiomatic: On arrival he sacrificed at Xu Ruzi's grave.

sentences.zh: 優待其後。

translations.literal: Generously treated his posterity.
translations.idiomatic: He cared for Xu's descendants.

sentences.zh: 禁其淫祀非禮之祭者。

translations.literal: Forbidden those excessive sacrifices not ritual sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He banned illicit shrines.

sentences.zh: 小吏資質佳者，輒令就學，擇其先進，擢置右職，舉善以教，風化大行。

translations.literal: Petty clerks with fine capacity—always ordered attend study—selected their advanced—promoted placed right offices—raising good to teach—custom transformation greatly practiced.
translations.idiomatic: He sent promising clerks to school, promoted the best, and spread decorum.

sentences.zh: 初，錢唐丁諝出於役伍，陽羨張秉生於庶民。

translations.literal: At first Qiantang Ding Xu emerged from labor ranks—Yangxian Zhang Bing born among common people.
translations.idiomatic: He lifted Ding Xu from the ranks and Zhang Bing from commoners.

sentences.zh: 烏程吳粲、雲陽殷禮起乎微賤，邵皆拔而友之，為立聲譽。

translations.literal: Wucheng Wu Can—Yunyang Yin Li rose from slight mean—Shao all pulled and befriended them—establishing fame reputation.
translations.idiomatic: He befriended Wu Can and Yin Li from humble roots.

sentences.zh: 秉遭大喪，親為制服結絰。

translations.literal: Bing encountered great mourning—personally for him made mourning garments tied headbands.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Bing mourned, Gu Shao wore hemp for him.

sentences.zh: 邵當之豫章，發在近路，值秉疾病，時送者百數。

translations.literal: When Shao went to Yuzhang—departure on near road—happened Bing illness—at time senders hundred count.
translations.idiomatic: Leaving for Yuzhang near home, Zhang Bing fell ill—hundreds came to see him off.

sentences.zh: 邵辭賓客曰："張仲節有疾，苦不能來別，恨不見之，暫還與訣，諸君少時相待。

translations.literal: Shao dismissed guests saying: "Zhang Zhongjie is ill—bitterly cannot come bid farewell—regrets not seeing him—temporarily return to bid farewell—gentlemen wait a short while."
translations.idiomatic: Gu Shao told guests: "Zhang Bing is too sick to say goodbye—I must see him—wait here briefly."

sentences.zh: "其留心下士，惟善所在，皆此類也。

translations.literal: " His mind attentive to inferiors—only where good lies—all this kind.
translations.idiomatic: He fussed over humble clients like this.

sentences.zh: 諝至典軍中郎，秉雲陽太守，禮零陵太守，

translations.literal: Xu reached Colonel of the Household Who Commands the Army—Bing Administrator of Yunyang—Li Administrator of Lingling—
translations.idiomatic: Ding Xu rose to colonel of the household army; Zhang Bing and Yin Li became prefects.

sentences.zh: 〈礼子基作通语曰：礼字德嗣，弱不好弄，潜识过人。

translations.literal: Li's son Ji authored Tongyu stating: Li courtesy name Desi—in youth did not play fondly—latent insight surpassed others.
translations.idiomatic: (Yin Li's son Yin Ji wrote Tongyu: Yin Li, styled Desi, was grave even as a boy.)

sentences.zh: 少为郡吏，年十九，守吴县丞。

translations.literal: Young became commandery clerk—age nineteen—acting Wu county assistant.
translations.idiomatic: At nineteen he was assistant magistrate of Wu.

sentences.zh: 孙权为王，召除郎中。

translations.literal: When Sun Quan became king—summoned removed Gentleman of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan as king named him gentleman of the palace.

sentences.zh: 后与张温俱使蜀，诸葛亮甚称叹之。

translations.literal: Later together with Zhang Wen both went as envoy to Shu—Zhuge Liang greatly praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Later he joined Zhang Wen's mission to Shu and impressed Zhuge Liang.

sentences.zh: 稍迁至零陵太守，卒官。

translations.literal: Gradually promoted reached Lingling prefect—died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Lingling prefect and died in harness.

sentences.zh: 文士传曰：礼子基，无难督，以才学知名，著通语数十篇。

translations.literal: Wenshi zhuan states: Li's son Ji—Colonel Who Has No Difficulty—by talent and learning became known—composed Tongyu several tens of chapters.
translations.idiomatic: (Wenshi zhuan: Yin Ji commanded the Feathered Forest and wrote Tongyu.)

sentences.zh: 有三子。

translations.literal: Had three sons.
translations.idiomatic: He had three sons.

sentences.zh: 巨字元大，有才器，初为吴偏将军，统家部曲，城夏口，吴平后，为苍梧太守。

translations.literal: Ju courtesy name Yuanda—had talent and capacity—first was Wu partial general—commanding household command—fortified Xiakou—after Wu pacified—became Cangwu prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Eldest Yin Ju became general and Cangwu prefect after Jin conquered Wu.

sentences.zh: 少子祐，字庆元，吴郡太守。〉

translations.literal: Youngest son You—courtesy name Qingyuan—Wu commandery prefect.〉
translations.idiomatic: Youngest Yin You was Wu prefect.)

sentences.zh: 粲太子少傅。

translations.literal: Can junior tutor to heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Can rose to junior tutor to the heir.

sentences.zh: 世以邵為知人。

translations.literal: The age considered Shao as knowing men.
translations.idiomatic: His generation called Gu Shao a judge of character.

sentences.zh: 在郡五年，卒官，子譚、承雲。

translations.literal: In commandery five years—died in office—sons Tan and Cheng cloud.
translations.idiomatic: After five years as prefect he died; sons Gu Tan and Gu Cheng survived.

sentences.zh: 邵子 譚

translations.literal: Shao's son Tan
translations.idiomatic: Gu Tan

sentences.zh: 譚字子默，弱冠與諸葛恪等為太子四友，從中庶子轉輔正都尉。

translations.literal: Tan courtesy name Zimo—at capping age together with Zhuge Ke and others were heir four friends—from gentleman attendant of heir transferred aide commandant who assists rectitude.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Tan, styled Zimo, was one of Sun Deng's four companions and became aide commandant.

sentences.zh: 〈陆机为谭传曰：宣太子正位东宫，天子方隆训导之义，妙简俊彦，讲学左右。

translations.literal: Lu Ji for Tan biography states: When Crown Prince came correct to eastern palace—Son of Heaven just then elevated instruction and guidance meaning—subtly selected brilliant talents—studying lecturing left and right.
translations.idiomatic: (Lu Ji's biography of Gu Tan: when Sun Deng took the eastern palace, the court packed his salon with talent.)

sentences.zh: 时四方之杰毕集，太傅诸葛恪等雄奇盖众，而谭以清识绝伦，独见推重。

translations.literal: At that time four quarters' heroes all gathered—Grand Tutor Zhuge Ke and others heroic strange surpassing host—yet Tan by pure insight unmatched—alone seen pushed weighty.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Ke dominated the heir's court, yet Gu Tan's clarity won highest esteem.

sentences.zh: 自太尉范慎、谢景、羊徽之徒，皆以秀称其名，而悉在谭下。〉

translations.literal: From Grand Commandant Fan Shen, Xie Jing, Yang Hui's cohort—all by excellence praised their names—yet all ranked below Tan.〉
translations.idiomatic: Men like Fan Shen lauded Gu Tan above themselves.)

sentences.zh: 赤烏中，代恪為左節度。

translations.literal: In Chiwu replaced Ke as left quartermaster.
translations.idiomatic: In Chiwu he succeeded Zhuge Ke as left quartermaster.

sentences.zh: 〈吴书曰：谭初践官府，上疏陈事，权辍食称善，以为过於徐详。

translations.literal: Wu shu states: Tan first treading official bureau—submitted memorial stating affairs—Quan stopped eating praising good—thought surpassed Xu Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: (Wu shu: Sun Quan skipped a meal praising his first memorial.)

sentences.zh: 雅性高亮，不脩意气，或以此望之。

translations.literal: By nature lofty bright—not cultivating temperament—some therefore blamed him.
translations.idiomatic: His lofty cold manner drew resentment.

sentences.zh: 然权鉴其能，见待甚隆，数蒙赏赐，特见召请。〉

translations.literal: Yet Quan mirrored his ability—treatment very lofty—repeatedly received rewards—specially summoned invited.〉
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan still favored and enriched him.)

translations.idiomatic: “These three—if their counsel fails, so be it—would they abuse majesty and bully their sovereign?”

translations.idiomatic: He also asked: “With rewards for good, punishments for evil, worthies in place, and law applied with clarity—what task would not succeed or sense fail?”

translations.idiomatic: Rash argument; rivalry for status; cliquishness; and reckless haste.

sentences.zh: 急論議則傷人，爭名勢則敗友，重朋黨則蔽主，務欲速則失德，此四者不除，未有能全也。

translations.literal: Hasty debate then harms people—strive fame power then defeats friends—weight faction then blinds lord—task desire speed then loses virtue—these four not removed—none able completely preserve.

translations.idiomatic: “Respectful and calm, awe-inspiring without harshness”—the chancellor walked it.

translations.idiomatic: “Learning not for pay, mind coveting nothing”—Yan Jun and Zhang Zhao practiced it.
